seo.title: Security — a policy your own browser verifies in front of you | Awalim Group
seo.description: We don't promise you security. We attack our own page five times while you watch and show you your browser refusing. A CSP with no unsafe-inline, enforced Trusted Types, and signed numbers.

h: We don't promise security. We attack ourselves in front of you.
lede: Every security page you have ever read is a list of promises. This one runs five real attacks against itself in your browser right now and shows you the browser refusing each one. If our policy ever weakens, this page will be the first thing to tell you.

live.lede: Not a simulation: each probe is the hostile action itself, and each verdict is read from the browser's own violation event or the exception the platform threw.

posture.lede: These are not settings written once and forgotten — the build generates them from the code that ships, so they cannot drift away from the page.

items.t: A hash for every inline script
items.d: No unsafe-inline in script-src. The build computes a SHA-256 of every inline script and puts it in the policy; change one character and the hash changes with it.
The site carried around 950 inline style attributes with only 74 distinct values between them. They are generated classes now, so unsafe-inline left style-src too.
Nine places that built HTML out of strings were removed — the worst of them passed your own typed words through. One named policy remains, and it can mint the service worker's URL and nothing else.
No fonts, scripts or images from a foreign origin. No tracking, no cookies, no analytics. What is never loaded can never be compromised.
Every public number is signed with an Ed25519 key at build time, and your browser is what verifies it — not our server.
What you type never passes through our server at all; it opens WhatsApp or your mail client on your own device.

honest.h: What this policy does not do
items: It does not protect you from a mistake in content we write and trust ourselves. It stops injection, not bad judgement.
It does not protect a device that is already compromised — a malicious browser extension comes before any policy.
The site is static, with no database and no accounts, so there is nothing in it to steal. That is not a virtue of ours; it is the shape of the site.

This page proves the policy you were served, and nothing more. If our host ever sent a header that differs from the one we declare, these five checks would still come back green for you. The build verifies the other side — that what is declared matches what ships — and the two together cover both ends.

Trusted Types is what actually refuses the eval and innerHTML probes — measured: adding unsafe-eval to the policy does not bring them back, because the platform refuses the sink before the content policy is consulted.

contact.d: Tell us directly and we answer within one working day. We have no bounty programme yet and will not pretend otherwise — but we credit whoever reports, if they want it.
